question.text: A body A of mass <math><mi>m</mi></math> is moving in a circular orbit of radius <math><mi>R</mi></math> about a planet. Another body B of mass <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> collides with A with a velocity which is half <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math> the instantaneous velocity <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> of A. The collision is completely inelastic. Then, the combined body:

options.text: continues to move in a circular orbit
Escapes from the Planet's Gravitational field
Falls vertically downwards towards the planet
starts moving in an elliptical orbit around the planet

solution.text:
Conserving momentum
m2v2+mv=m+m2vf
vf=2mV4×3m2=5V6
vf<vorb=v thus the combined mass will go on to an elliptical path
